name: CONTENT-COMMENT-AND-EVENTS
status: candidate implementation; H2 and synthetic loopback fixtures only; real MySQL/User/Redis and consumer integration unverified

write.authentication: verified JWT and live authoritative session with blog scope; actor comes only from principal
write.rules: type 0 article or 1 friend; rootId -1 for roots; numeric or decimal-string integer IDs accepted; fractions and overflow rejected. Root toCommentId and toCommentUserId may be null or -1. A reply requires positive rootId and toCommentId; supplied toCommentUserId must match the actual target author. Ignore client id/actor/audit/deleted fields.
write.friendSentinel: For type 1, absent/null/0 and exact historical sentinel 1 normalize to articleId null; any other positive articleId is invalid. Sentinel 1 never selects an article or an article notification recipient.

read.parameters: articleId required positive for article reads; friend read accepts absent/null/0/1 as the same independent space. pageNum default 1; pageSize default 10, maximum 100; offset maximum 10000000.
read.shape: data has rows, total decimal string, profileLookupLimited boolean. Root comments paginate by createdAt/id; children are ordered by rootId/createdAt/id and include only current-page roots and same visible scope. Existing CommentVo fields use camelCase, long IDs as decimal strings and GMT+8 yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss; username and toCommentUserName may be null with userInfoStatus/toCommentUserInfoStatus FOUND/MISSING/UNAVAILABLE. Content is original text.
read.budget: Per request at most 100 roots and independently at most 500 children. More than 500 children returns HTTP 413/code 515 without a partial success. At most 100 distinct profile IDs are looked up in one bounded batch; if more are needed, unqueried profiles are UNAVAILABLE and profileLookupLimited=true while all comments are returned. Empty page performs no User call. A future thread paging flow is needed for oversized threads.

api.errors: Empty content HTTP 200/code 506; invalid thread/input HTTP 200/code 515; missing/draft/withdrawn/deleted article HTTP 200/code 513; commenting disabled HTTP 403/code 403; malformed JSON or numeric overflow/fraction HTTP 400/code 400; limiter unavailable HTTP 503/code 500; limiter denial HTTP 429/code 429 and Retry-After seconds.
api.content: Maximum 4000 UTF-16 units; blank, NUL and malformed surrogate sequences rejected. Stored and returned as original text. Browser clients must render as text; the authorized message.vue component uses Vue interpolation and fixed local emoji assets instead of v-html.

transactions.write: READ COMMITTED transaction takes content_write_fence first, locks the article then root/target comments in ascending ID order. It verifies public/not-deleted article and isComment=1, plus same type, scope and actual root relationship. Comment and immutable event commit together; no external service is called while holding the fence.
transactions.read: READ COMMITTED transaction takes the same fence, checks visibility and reads page plus children before release; the subsequent User profile lookup is outside the transaction. A response racing a withdrawal is linearized at the DB snapshot and may complete after withdrawal. All future article/comment writers must follow this fence protocol.
transactions.limits: No comment write-count cap is imposed by the read budget. Fence serialization may reduce throughput; no global snapshot/export guarantee is made.

events.identity: One immutable event per new comment, eventId UUID, aggregateType COMMENT, aggregateId/commentId decimal strings, independent sourceRevision 1; no change to article revision or article facts.
events.semantics: rootCommentId and toCommentId use -1 for roots. Article root receiver is article author; article reply receiver is actual target author. Friend events use null articleId and null receiverId and must not enter the future article-notification channel. Preview is at most 500 Unicode code points; full body and session/token data are excluded. Validated request ID is carried as correlationId. Consumers must escape preview when rendering. Relay, delivery and deduplication by consumers remain future work.

rules: 10 admitted valid-shaped attempts per user in a 60-second fixed window
30 admitted valid-shaped attempts per direct socket peer in a 60-second fixed window
1 admitted valid-shaped attempt for the same user and exact content in a 30-second fixed window
rateLimit.behavior: Database-clock fixed windows begin with the first admitted attempt; three keys are locked in stable order and updated atomically in a separate transaction before the content transaction. Invalid business target or later write failure still consumes an admitted attempt. A rejected limit check does not create a comment. This is anti-abuse, not durable request idempotency.
rateLimit.storage: Only SHA-256 pseudonyms, hit counts and expiry timestamps are retained in content_comment_limit; hashes are pseudonyms, not encryption. Each request removes at most 100 expired rows before checking; cleanup is request-triggered, so expired rows may remain during idle periods.
rateLimit.peer: Use only servlet direct numeric socket peer; server.forward-headers-strategy=none. Forwarded and X-Forwarded-For are ignored. Behind a Gateway, users sharing its egress address share the IP quota until a separately approved trusted-proxy contract is implemented.

schema: Manual new-install content-article-schema.sql or 02C/02D-only content-comment-03a-upgrade.sql; never auto-applied. Tables content_comment, content_comment_event, content_comment_limit and thread/expiry indexes. Native MySQL DDL and query plans remain unverified.
verification: Local H2 MySQL-mode and loopback Content/User provider fixtures with synthetic credentials; deterministic lock interleavings, rate concurrency, rollback and limits. Frontend regression renders the authorized Vue component in Jest/jsdom. No real OSS/User/Redis/MySQL or downstream relay/consumer integration.
deferred: real Gateway peer identity and native MySQL concurrency/DDL
